questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which of the following is a false rib?
questions.explanation: The 8th rib is a false rib because it does not articulate with the sternum anteriorly. The source classifies ribs 1-7 as true ribs, ribs 8-10 as false ribs because they join the superjacent costal cartilage, and ribs 11-12 as floating ribs because they float freely without costal attachment.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which of the following joints is not formed by direct articulation with ribs?
questions.explanation: The costosternal joint is not formed by direct articulation of a rib with the sternum; it is formed by articulation of the lateral sternal border with the costal cartilage. Costovertebral and costotransverse joints directly involve ribs, and the costochondral joint is at the rib-costal cartilage junction.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: What type of joint is the first sternocostal joint?
questions.explanation: The source gives the first sternocostal joint as a synarthrosis, i.e. a no-movement joint in the functional classification. It also reviews structural joint classification: fibrous joints include sutures, syndesmoses and gomphoses; cartilaginous joints include synchondroses and symphyses; synovial joints are freely movable.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: The joint between the attachment of the 8th and 9th rib to the 7th rib is a:
questions.explanation: The interchondral joint between the attachment of the 8th and 9th rib with the 7th rib is a synovial joint. The source reviews thoracic-cavity joint types: first sternocostal joint is a fibrous/synarthrosis relation, costochondral joints are synchondroses, manubriosternal and xiphisternal joints are symphyses, and interchondral/costovertebral/costotransverse joints are synovial. It notes that the interchondral joint between the 9th and 10th cartilages is never synovial and may be absent.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which of the following does not provide articulations to ribs?
questions.explanation: The spinous processes of vertebrae do not provide articulations to the ribs. The source notes that the two facets on the head of a typical rib are separated by a transverse crest that attaches to the intervertebral disc above it.

questions.question: Which of the following ribs is atypical and doesn't articulate with the vertebra at 3 sites?
questions.explanation: The first rib is atypical and does not articulate with a vertebra at three sites; it has two articulations in the source description: a circular facet on the head with the body of the first thoracic vertebra and the tubercle with the transverse process of the corresponding vertebra. questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: A 47-year-old smoker presented with cough, chest pain, dyspnea, and right shoulder pain. Chest X-ray revealed homogeneous opacity at the lung apex and destruction of the first rib. Which of the following structures is not compressed?
questions.explanation: The source identifies the picture as a Pancoast tumor at the apex of the right lung. Structures between the first rib and the apex of the lung are compressed, but the thoracic duct is not listed among them. From medial to lateral the source gives the mnemonic SVAN: sympathetic trunk, vein (posterior intercostal), artery (superior intercostal), nerve (T1). Pancoast tumors can destroy the first rib by mass effect.

questions.question: The image given below shows structures in the posterior triangle of the neck. Where does the structure marked A attach?
questions.explanation: Structure A is scalenus anterior. It attaches to the first rib at the scalene tubercle. The source notes that the scalene tubercle is a small projection on the medial border of the first rib between the anterior and posterior grooves. It also contrasts tuberculum sellae as a sphenoid-bone part and Chassaignac's/carotid tubercle as a feature of the C6 transverse process.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: The relationship of the components of the neurovascular bundle from below upwards in intercostal space is _______.
questions.explanation: From below upward the intercostal neurovascular bundle is arranged nerve-artery-vein. From above downward the familiar mnemonic is VAN: vein, artery, nerve.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which among the following is incorrect regarding Sibson's fascia?

options.text: Attached to the inner border of 2nd rib

questions.correctAnswerText: Attached to the inner border of 2nd rib
questions.explanation: The incorrect statement is that Sibson's fascia attaches to the inner border of the second rib. The source describes Sibson's fascia (suprapleural membrane) as a fascial plane separating lower neck and thorax, covering the lung apex and attaching to the inner border of the first rib and posteriorly to the anterior border of the transverse process of C7. It is strengthened by fibers derived from scalenus minimus, and the subclavian vessels lie on top of it.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: On the ides of March, Julius Caesar was stabbed 23 times. One such stab wound was present in the left supraclavicular fossa, piercing his left lung. Which of the following provides the vertebral attachment of the fascia present here?
questions.explanation: The stabbed lung apex is covered by Sibson's fascia (suprapleural membrane). The source states that its vertebral attachment is posteriorly to the anterior border of the transverse process of the C7 vertebra; anteriorly it attaches to the inner border of the first rib.
